text.p: Citrix Systems Inc. faces yet another class action lawsuit alleging that the networking software company misled shareholders about potential competition from Microsoft Corp., plaintiffs' lawyers said Friday.
The complaint charges that Citrix and four of its officers and directors failed to disclose information regarding rivalry from Microsoft, and that they falsely denied rumours about the rivalry.

The complaint also alleges that while in possession of this information, the defendants sold over 71,000 shares of common stock at prices of $45 to $50 per share, for total proceeds of over $3.39 million.

Fort Lauderdale, Fla.-based Citrix's stock fell almost 60 percent on Feb. 27 amid concerns that its core product might face competition from Microsoft. It rose 34.38 cents to $14.56 on Nasdaq in late trading.
Citirx said it had no comment on the suit.
The complaint was filed by the firm of Burt & Pucillo, of West Palm Beach, and follows a similar lawsuit announced on March 10.
